sections.h2: How did a farm stop called Wellston become Warner Robins?
sections.html:
A railroad stop with a sawmill, a grocery and peach orchards, Wellston held only about 50 people in 1940. Then the War Department picked Houston County for an air depot, and on September 1, 1942 the community took the name Warner Robins, after an Air Corps general. It became a town in March 1943 and a city in 1956, per Wikipedia.

Growth since then has been steep: 7,986 residents in 1950, 33,491 in 1970, 66,588 in 2010 and 80,308 in 2020, with an estimate of 87,761 for 2025. Robins Air Force Base sits just east of the city line across U.S. 129 and supplies more than 25,000 military, civil service and contractor jobs. The city covers about 38 square miles, lies 20 miles south of Macon and 100 miles south of Atlanta, and spreads across Houston and Peach counties.

Houston County Schools run the public side of town: Houston County High, Warner Robins High, Northside High, Houston College and Career Academy and an alternative academy called WIN, with Veterans High in nearby Kathleen. Middle Georgia State College and Central Georgia Technical College keep branch campuses here, and the Nola Brantley Memorial Library is the city library.

Roads shape where people live. U.S. 129 and Georgia 247 run along the east side, Interstate 75 sits about 6 miles west, and Georgia 96 crosses the southern edge. The Museum of Aviation next to the base is a major visitor draw, and Warner Robins American Little League won the 2007 Little League World Series.

Tornadoes are part of local memory. An F4 storm struck on April 30, 1953, killing 18 people, and the area's tornado activity has since run above the state average. Summers are hot and humid, with a record high of 108 degrees in July.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about homes in Warner Robins?
sections.html:
Owners occupy barely over half the homes here. QuickFacts puts the owner-occupied rate at 53.5% for 2020-2024, well below the 65.2% national rate.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $185,700, against $332,700 nationally.
  • Median gross rent: $1,212.
  • Median household income: $66,970 across 31,930 households.
  • Veterans: 8,651.
  • Residents 65 and older: 11.9%, compared with 18.9% nationally.

In 2020, 34,191 units stood in the city, and 7.4% were empty. Median age was 34.1 and 26.3% of residents were under 18, while 99.8% lived in urban areas, which marks a young, built-up city with a big rental market. The numbers come from the Census Bureau.

sections.h2: Which governments tax a Warner Robins house?
sections.html:
Houston County, the Houston County school system, the state and the City of Warner Robins each take a share. Houston County dates from May 15, 1821, and its seat is Perry, on a 380-square-mile territory. Cities inside it are Warner Robins, Perry, Centerville and part of Byron.

Countywide the 2020 census counted 66,633 housing units, 6.8% of them vacant, with 64.3% of the occupied ones owner-occupied. The county's population climbed from 110,765 in 2000 to 139,900 in 2010 and 163,633 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 178,214. Interstate 75, U.S. 41, U.S. 129, U.S. 341 and Georgia 96 are among its major routes.

A smaller slice of Warner Robins lies in Peach County and is served by the Peach County School District, so owners with a Peach County parcel should ask the Peach County Tax Commissioner how their bill is handled.

  • Houston County Tax Commissioner, Warner Robins office: 202 Carl Vinson Parkway, Warner Robins, GA 31088; (478) 542-2110; weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
  • Perry office: 201 Perry Parkway, (478) 218-4940.
  • Email for real property questions: taxquestions@houstoncountyga.gov.
  • Houston County Tax Assessors, 201 Perry Parkway in Perry: (478) 218-4750 for real estate, with parcel data on qPublic.
  • City of Warner Robins billing questions: (478) 929-1148, as the assessors' FAQ lists it.

The assessors say they do not handle billing, and the commissioner says it does not set value or millage.

sections.h2: What millage rate has the City of Warner Robins set?
sections.html:
On September 22, 2026 the Mayor and Council adopted 10.000 mills for the 2026 tax year, up 1.047 mills from the 8.953 rate used in 2024 and 2025, according to the city's announcement.

Houston County voters approved a Floating Homestead Local Option Sales Tax in May 2026, and the city expects 2028 to be the first full calendar year of that revenue. County and school rates are separate and appear on your own statement.

sections.h2: When does Houston County collect Warner Robins property tax?
sections.html:
Houston County mails real estate statements ahead of October 20, and December 20 is the due date. The office accepts partial payments. Interest builds each month at the legal rate, and every 120 days adds a 5% penalty until the penalties reach 20%.

According to the commissioner's FAQ, a lien may be recorded once tax is more than 90 days overdue, while a levy is held back as a last resort. Manufactured homes keep their own calendar: January bills, April 1 due date, decal on payment, and a 10% penalty for late payment.

Statements are mailed to the homeowner and never to the lender. Borrowers who escrow need to send the bill along themselves.

sections.h2: What exemptions and appeal rights apply in Houston County?
sections.html:
New homestead filings go to the Houston County Tax Assessor's Office and must arrive by April 1. First-time owners should bring a copy of the warranty deed. Once approved, the exemption continues until ownership or residence changes.

  • Age 65 and older, combined with another homestead exemption: relief from the state portion of tax on the house and as much as 10 acres.
  • Gross household income of $15,000 or less, age 62 and up: tax deferral.
  • Real property returns and conservation-use requests: mailed, with a postmark of April 1 at the latest.

To challenge a value, write to the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the notice. From there the path runs through the Board of Equalization (or arbitration) and, if needed, Superior Court. Complaints about the size of the bill are outside the appeal.

sections.h2: What should a Warner Robins seller know before closing?
sections.html:
Call the commissioner's Warner Robins office for a payoff and hand the figure to your closing attorney or title company. Value is fixed as of January 1 each year, so the sale contract should state how the year's bill is divided.

Landlords should check personal property too. The assessors warn that people who buy a business, boat or aircraft sometimes find years of unpaid tax afterward, and that attorneys usually review only the real estate side.

If you inherited the house, fell behind or live elsewhere, a buyer taking the house as it is can pay the county out of the proceeds, with no repairs or showings on your end.

faqs.q: What is the due date for property tax in Warner Robins?
faqs.a: December 20. Statements go out before October 20, and manufactured homes are billed separately for April 1.

faqs.q: What millage did Warner Robins adopt for 2026?
faqs.a: 10.000 mills, adopted September 22, 2026, after 8.953 mills in both 2024 and 2025.

faqs.q: Where can I pay in person in Warner Robins?
faqs.a: At the Houston County Tax Commissioner's office, 202 Carl Vinson Parkway, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. An online payment adds a convenience fee.

faqs.q: Who reviews a Houston County value dispute first?
faqs.a: The Board of Tax Assessors, reached at (478) 218-4750 for real estate. The notice gives you 45 days.

faqs.q: Do Peach County parcels in Warner Robins go to Houston County?
faqs.a: No. That slice of the city is served by Peach County's offices, so ask the Peach County Tax Commissioner how the parcel is billed.
